metadata.title: Trump says China obtained 220 million US voter files ahead of 2020 election

content.text:
Investing.com -- President Donald Trump said China illicitly acquired 220 million US voter files beginning during the 2020 election cycle, calling the alleged breach an "unprecedented election security nightmare" in a Truth Social post on Friday.
Trump said the compromised information included names, addresses, telephone numbers, and political affiliations. He also claimed China assigned a data exploitation unit to the project.
The allegations draw on newly declassified intelligence released by the administration. The documents describe vulnerabilities in voter registration databases, electronic poll books, and election websites that foreign adversaries could exploit.
No evidence has emerged showing that China used the voter information to alter ballots or vote totals. A review of the documents found that they did not overturn earlier intelligence conclusions that no foreign country directly manipulated the 2020 result. China called the allegations "groundless" and denied interfering in US elections.
Election security is becoming a major Republican campaign issue ahead of November's midterms. Trump has called on Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, which would require documentary proof of US citizenship for voter registration.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin separately said federal officials had identified more than 250,000 potentially ineligible voters in California, New Jersey, Nevada, and Pennsylvania.
Mullin gave the four states two weeks to review their voter rolls and warned that election officials could face fines, penalties, or criminal charges for failing to act. The department did not publicly provide evidence supporting its figures or explain the criteria used to compile them.
Nevada Secretary of State Francisco Aguilar rejected the numbers as speculative and unsupported. Pennsylvania said it would review the information but maintained that noncitizen voting is extremely rare.
The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency plans to release an updated election infrastructure plan within 30 days.
